free_tier.stated: no free tier or free credit is stated on the pages read: billing is per second against a credit balance that must be funded before a machine can be rented.

per_object_cap.notes: a machine record: vCPU, RAM and local storage per GPU vary by offer

retention.stated: a stopped pod keeps its environment and volume in managed storage at USD 0.02 per GiB per 30-day month until it is deleted
retention.notes: held storage bills until the pod is deleted

egress.terms: Network egress and ingress policy is set by each on-demand provider individually and is not uniform across the marketplace.

interface_detail: an `aq` CLI covers the console surface and `aq ssh <name>` writes an SSH alias; a REST API was not found on the pages read
tooling: the `aq` CLI (`aq ssh`, `aq stop`, `aq start`, `aq down`) and a web console; a stopped pod can be restarted on a different card or provider
chaining: One account and one balance across several GPU providers, billed per second, with a pod (environment plus volume) that survives a stop and can restart on another provider. The price is a live minimum across current supply, so it moves between page loads.

limits.value: the credit balance is the quota: credit must be on the account before any machine is rented, and usage draws it down per second; list prices are live minimums refreshed every 6 hours

limits_note: no free allowance; the on-demand list price is a live minimum and an L4 had no on-demand supply when read
binding_note: no free allowance; the on-demand list price is a live minimum and an L4 had no on-demand supply when read

identity_cost.detail: Signup needs an email address that is verified; renting needs credit on the account, added by card or by Solana. Whether the card route asks for a billing address, a phone number or an ID check is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: preemptible offers run on hardware contributed by independent hosts, so they can be taken back; on-demand offers run in operator-managed facilities

evidence.proved: H100 on-demand list rate USD 2.78 per GPU-hour, live range 2.78 to 5.32

evidence.quote: The cheapest current on-demand rate for the L40S on Aquanode is $1.07/GPU/hr. Live rates range from $0.881 to $3.81 per GPU per hour
evidence.proved: L40S on-demand USD 1.07 per GPU-hour, live range 0.881 to 3.81

evidence.proved: L4 at USD 1.10 per GPU-hour, with no on-demand supply at the time read

evidence.quote: Live prices for every GPU you can rent on Aquanode, refreshed every 6 hours. Billed per second, with no contracts and no minimum term.
evidence.proved: prices are live and refreshed every 6 hours, billed per second with no contract or minimum term

evidence.quote: Every offer on Aquanode is tagged on-demand or preemptible. On-demand capacity runs in operator-managed facilities with consistent uptime expectations; preemptible compute is real, often cheaper, hardware contributed by independent hosts.
evidence.proved: offers are on-demand or preemptible, and preemptible hardware belongs to independent hosts

evidence.quote: and verify your email. You will need credit on the account before you can rent a machine
evidence.proved: signup needs a verified email address, and credit on the account before a machine can be rented

evidence.proved: egress terms vary by the underlying provider of each offer

evidence.quote: Holding them in Aquanode's managed storage bills at $0.02 per GiB per 30-day month, metered per second.
evidence.proved: held environment and volume storage is USD 0.02 per GiB per 30-day month

evidence.proved: machines are reached with the aq CLI and plain SSH

notes: A marketplace over several GPU hosts. On-demand list rates per GPU-hour read on the vendor's pages (live, refreshed every 6 hours): H100 80GB USD 2.78; A100 80GB USD 1.49; L40S 48GB USD 1.07; RTX 4090 24GB USD 0.760; L4 24GB USD 1.10 with no on-demand supply at the time (the cheapest offer overall). Including preemptible offers the per-model pages quote a lower floor: A100 USD 1.23, L40S USD 0.881, RTX 4090 USD 0.394. The pricing page lists 15 GPU models priced on-demand; a third-party index lists 38.
